chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, concerning:

A man prays over two deceased persons or three dead persons—how should he pray over them? He said: If they are three, or two, or ten, or more than that, then let him perform one salat over them, saying five takbirs over them, just as he prays over one deceased person. Whoever prays over them all together should place one deceased person, then place the other next to the buttocks of the first, then place the head of the third next to the buttocks of the second, in a stair-like arrangement, until he has arranged all of them, whatever their number may be. When he has arranged them like that, he stands in the middle and pronounces five takbirs, doing as he does when he prays over one deceased person. He was asked: What if the dead are men and women? He said: He begins with the men, placing the head of the second next to the buttocks of the first, until he has finished arranging all the men. Then he places the head of the woman next to the buttocks of the last man, then places the head of the other woman next to the buttocks of the first woman, until he has arranged all of them. When they have been arranged in this way, he stands in the middle, in the midst of the men, and pronounces takbir over them as he prays over one deceased person.
Thus, the proper way regarding these reports is to regard the matter as one of choice, because acting upon whichever of them it may be is permissible; this indicates that.

key_terms.التَّخْيِيرُ: the allowance of choice between reported permissible forms
key_terms.الرِّجَالِ: the male deceased, who are arranged first
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the female deceased in the arrangement of the funeral line
key_terms.الْوَسَطِ: the middle position where the one praying stands
key_terms.خَمْسَ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ: five takbirs recited in the funeral prayer
key_terms.صَلَاةً وَاحِدَةً: a single funeral prayer performed for multiple deceased persons

ai.seo_question: How should salat be performed over multiple deceased persons together according to al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for performing salat over multiple deceased persons together in a single funeral prayer. It describes how their bodies are to be arranged, including when men and women are present together, and indicates that the reports on this matter allow for permissibility through choice among the transmitted forms.
